newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians vote in local ballot runoff.
newsitem.headline: Albanians vote in local ballot runoff.

text.p: Voting was under way in parts of Albania on Sunday in a run-off to elect leaders of 22 town halls and 96 communes where no candidate won a majority in last weekend's local polls.

The ruling Democratic Party took 88 percent of city halls in the first round vote last Sunday, up from 51 percent in 1992 elections. They also won in 62.5 percent of communes, up from 37 percent, and 52.5 percent of the vote for regional councils compared with 43 percent last time.

The key opposition Socialists won 9.5 percent of city halls, down from 35 percent, and 3.9 percent of communes, down from 45 percent. They gained 31 percent of the vote for regional councils, compared with 41 percent in 1992.
The official results decide the political make-up of 42 city halls, 212 communes and 36 regional councils.

The polls were considered a litmus test for Albania's fledgling democracy after a controversial general election in May and June was boycotted by most opposition parties, which alleged the ballot was rigged in favour of the Democrats.
The Democratic Party daily Rilindja Demokratike said in an editorial it was important that the "civilisation and high democratic level shown last Sunday be repeated today".
The opposition Socialist Party called on its voters to take part in the poll.
"We appeal to the electors: let's go to the polls to repair (the damage of) October 20," Socialist secretary general Rexhep Mejdani said.
The Socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, have criticised the way the poll was conducted but most independent observers have concluded it was fair.
